requirements.summary: U1 pins match the AMS1117 datasheet: pin 1 GND/ADJ to GND, pin 2 VOUT to the +3V3 net, pin 3 VIN to +5V. The ESP-12F module pins use the KiCad RF_Module:ESP-12F symbol, but no ESP-12F datasheet is in the bundle (only the ESP8266EX chip and WROOM-02 datasheets), so the module pinout cannot be checked against its own datasheet. The HLK-PM01 and G5RL relay pinouts cannot be checked either: there is no HLK-PM01 datasheet, and the Omron PDF failed text extraction.

The strapping topology is correct. GPIO15 is pulled down by R5 to GND. GPIO0 and GPIO2 are pulled up by R3 and R4. EN has R1 pull-up plus C7, and RST has R2 pull-up plus C8. However, every pull-up goes to the +3V3 net, which U1 (AMS1117-1.8) actually holds at 1.8 V. That is below the ESP8266 2.5 V minimum working voltage, so normal start-up will not happen even though the strap levels are logically right.

requirements.summary: U1 is a fixed 1.8 V AMS1117 (AMS1117-1.8), but it drives the +3V3 rail that powers the ESP-12F VCC pin. 1.8 V is below the ESP8266EX working range of 2.5 to 3.6 V, so the module will not run or will behave erratically. The deterministic check CIR-REG-001 also flags this mismatch.

evidence.quote: U1 (AMS1117-1.8) outputs 1.8 V on rail +3V3 (3.3 V)

requirements.summary: The mains input has F1 (T500mA) in series with L ahead of PS1, and RV1 across L_F and N after the fuse, which is a reasonable topology for a 3 W HLK-PM01. However, RV1 is a 07D221K (220 V varistor voltage). A 221K part is normally rated for only about 140 VAC continuous, so on 230 VAC mains it would conduct continuously and fail. A 471K part is typical for 230 V. The mains voltage is not stated, and no varistor datasheet is provided. The relay load path (L_IN to K1.13 to L_OUT) is unfused on the board.

The U1 regulator value is wrong for its function: an AMS1117-1.8 is fitted on a rail named +3V3 that feeds a 3.3 V module. The symbol (AMS1117-3.3) and the value (AMS1117-1.8) also disagree. The other values look reasonable: 10k pull-ups, 1k base resistor with a 10k pull-down, 1k LED resistor, 220 ohm LED resistor, and a 1N4148W flyback diode across the coil.

The U1 SOT-223 footprint matches the AMS1117 SOT-223 package, and the ESP-12E footprint is pin-compatible with the ESP-12F. K1 is valued as an Omron G5RL-1A-E-HR, but it uses the G2RL-1A-E footprint, and the G5RL datasheet could not be read to confirm the pad layout. No footprint is on an approved list yet (PCB-FOOT-001 WARN), and the LCSC codes cannot be checked offline.

extra_findings.text: error: The BOM and the schematic disagree on U1. The value is AMS1117-1.8, but the symbol is AMS1117-3.3, and the same LCSC code C6186 is ordered (C6186 is commonly the AMS1117-3.3 listing). What JLCPCB actually places is ambiguous. Pick one part (AMS1117-3.3 for this design) and make the value, symbol and LCSC code agree.

warning: Pin 2 of the programming header J3 is tied to +5V, the HLK-PM01 output. If a USB-UART adapter powers the board through this pin, it back-feeds the AC-DC module's output. If the board is programmed while mains is connected, the header is not isolated from mains-powered circuitry. Consider supplying 3V3 instead, or adding a warning on the silkscreen.
